title: [GOVERNANCE] Enforce main and development protection and invite the second developer
scope: Establish development as integration and main as production, preserve merge commits, resolve the protection API denial, verify enforceable PR gates and invite the confirmed collaborator.
acceptance: Feature pull requests target development and only an accepted development release promotes to main
Read back active protection/rules and required checks on both long-lived branches
Merge commits are enabled while squash and rebase merges remain disabled
Record collaborator invitation/acceptance only after the owner supplies the username
tests: Settings read-back and a controlled pull-request/check enforcement test after protection becomes available.
risk: Incorrect access changes can weaken controls or block both developers. Change one control at a time and revert only the specific mistaken setting.

title: [CONTENT] Establish the approved source and licensing registry
scope: Select works and editions consistent with organizer guidance, documenting approval and rights separately from API availability.
acceptance: Every approved source has author/work/edition/reference and rights evidence
A qualified content reviewer confirms the bounded source-selection policy
tests: Registry completeness, rejected/withdrawn source cases and manual attribution review.
risk: Unlicensed or unsuitable material must not enter the corpus. Remove unapproved entries and rebuild affected indexes.

title: [CONTENT] Curate 30–50 contextual reference passages
scope: Build a small rights-approved corpus that preserves Arabic originals, conditions, attribution and neighboring context.
acceptance: Passages have stable IDs, edition links, hashes and reviewer approval
Coverage and exclusions are documented; no claim of comprehensive Islamic coverage
tests: Context/negation preservation and source-reference spot checks.
risk: Truncated context can reverse meaning. Withdraw affected passages and invalidate dependent evaluations.

title: [DATA] Implement Neon schema, migrations and guest ownership
scope: Implement the proposed relational model in an isolated Neon environment, including revisions, runs, evidence and expiring guest sessions.
acceptance: Reviewed migrations reproduce the schema in a clean non-production database
Cross-session access is denied and revision/run relationships are enforced
tests: Migration apply/compatibility, foreign-key, ownership, expiration and deletion tests.
risk: Data loss or exposure. Use isolated synthetic data and reviewed expand-and-contract/forward-fix; no destructive production operations.

title: [RAG] Implement versioned embedding ingestion
scope: Embed approved passages with explicit model, dimension, task type and corpus version; evaluate the proposed Cohere candidate.
acceptance: Ingestion preserves provenance and original Arabic
Incompatible embedding models/configurations cannot share a query space
tests: Idempotent ingestion, interrupted batch recovery, model/dimension mismatch and mocked provider failures.
risk: Unexpected costs or incompatible vectors. Bound batches and retain a lexical-only fallback; rebuild a separate index when models change.

title: [RAG] Implement hybrid retrieval and evidence recall evaluation
scope: Combine exact reference lookup, lexical candidates and compatible semantic retrieval, restoring source context.
acceptance: Only approved source editions reach the evidence bundle
Compare lexical, vector and hybrid retrieval on held-out reviewer-labeled passages
tests: Reference resolution, Recall@5, context restoration, duplicate-source and unavailable-embedding cases.
risk: Relevant evidence can be missed. Disclose degraded retrieval and abstain where evidence is insufficient.

title: [API] Integrate Tafsir MCP with an approved snapshot fallback
scope: Implement a typed MCP adapter after verifying live tool schemas, chosen source editions and caching rights.
acceptance: Record successful permitted calls with pinned schemas and source versions
A licensed same-edition snapshot path is tested or explicitly marked unavailable
tests: Schema contract, timeout, malformed response, missing reference and fallback attribution tests.
risk: Endpoint/version changes or unsuitable tafsir selection. Disable the adapter and use only approved disclosed evidence.

title: [API] Verify authorized Dorar access and bounded hadith coverage
scope: Obtain the supported access/schema/terms and validate from the intended backend environment; legacy PHP/JS wrappers are not independent backups.
acceptance: Document successful authorized JSON responses or keep live integration disabled
Preserve named scholar/source attribution and disclose limited fallback coverage
tests: Controlled happy-path and 403/429/HTML challenge tests; do not report uptime from a small access probe.
risk: Access denial must not become a false hadith verdict. Disable live feature and route unresolved cases for review.

title: [CORE] Extract claims and obtain editor confirmation
scope: Extract bounded claims, quotations and references with original offsets, then require editor confirmation.
acceptance: Structured output retains revision-linked spans
Editors can correct/remove extracted claims before paid assessment
tests: Mixed text, nested quotes, ambiguity, malicious instructions and invalid structured output.
risk: Extraction can change meaning. Preserve original text and require confirmation; fall back to manual claim selection.

title: [CORE] Implement deterministic quotation and attribution checks
scope: Compare quotations with approved source text using exact and explicitly limited normalization; keep attribution distinct.
acceptance: Original source text remains unchanged
Negation, omitted conditions and incorrect references are not normalized into a match
tests: Exact, diacritics, punctuation, ellipsis, wrong verse and missing source fixtures.
risk: Over-normalization can conceal meaning changes. Use conservative unresolved status and reviewer inspection.

title: [CORE] Assess claim support with evidence and scope guards
scope: Implement bounded assessment of generalization, omitted qualification and exclusivity using only the retrieved evidence bundle.
acceptance: Every concrete finding resolves to approved evidence and the current revision
Invalid citations, unsupported output and out-of-scope requests abstain or require review
tests: Correct quote/unsupported inference, invented IDs, stale revisions, insufficient evidence and disagreement.
risk: Plausible model reasoning can be wrong. Require scientific evaluation and disable categories failing critical cases.

title: [API] Implement review orchestration and recoverable run state
scope: Connect confirmed revisions, retrieval, checks and findings with persistent state and bounded execution.
acceptance: Idempotency prevents duplicate logical runs
Timeouts/restarts produce recoverable or explicitly interrupted states; no untracked background promises
tests: Duplicate submission, late result, cancellation, restart and exhausted-budget integration tests.
risk: Duplicate costs or incorrect lifecycle. Preserve immutable run records and stop affected processing safely.

title: [UX] Build the Arabic intake and claim-confirmation flow
scope: Implement welcome, privacy/scope disclosure, draft input and editable claim confirmation without mandatory accounts.
acceptance: Empty/oversized/out-of-scope states are understandable
Keyboard and RTL operation preserve original text and user corrections
tests: Component and browser tests for input, validation, focus, mobile layout and API errors.
risk: User may mistake prototype for complete verification. Retain explicit capability/coverage disclosures.

title: [UX] Build evidence-linked reports, revisions and review export
scope: Show separate quotation/support findings, source context, suggested edits and a downloadable unresolved-case packet.
acceptance: Each finding opens its exact evidence and limitation
Edits create new revisions; export does not promise a live scholar service
tests: Evidence navigation, stale outputs, undo/recheck, partial report and export completeness.
risk: A simplified badge may imply religious approval. Use explicit bounded labels and reject unsupported summaries.

title: [RELIABILITY] Implement bounded retries, caching and fallback
scope: Add timeout budgets, circuit breaking, allowed caching and capability-aware fallback without changing source identity silently.
acceptance: 401/403 are not blindly retried; transient failures respect budgets
Different-source or lexical-only fallback is disclosed and reassessed
tests: Failure injection across provider/model/embedding paths, cache-version and breaker recovery tests.
risk: Fallback may appear successful while losing evidence quality. Return partial/insufficient results instead of invented completeness.

title: [EVALUATION] Build the reviewed benchmark and comparative report
scope: Implement the test strategy with held-out reviewer-labeled cases and fair manual-search/general-model baselines.
acceptance: Publish actual sample counts, per-class results, failures and uncertainty
Keep development fixtures separate from held-out scientific evaluation
tests: Reproducible evaluator, metric calculation checks and manual review of critical errors.
risk: Inflated accuracy or biased baselines. Predeclare criteria and retain negative results; block unsupported claims.

title: [SECURITY] Verify privacy, ownership and untrusted-input controls
scope: Implement and verify guest isolation, deletion, safe rendering, allowlisted fetches, prompt-injection boundaries and log redaction.
acceptance: No cross-session report access and no sensitive content in logs
HTML, arbitrary URLs and embedded instructions cannot escalate privileges
tests: IDOR, XSS, SSRF, injection, expiration and deletion negative cases.
risk: User data exposure. Keep real-user deployment blocked until verified; revoke exposed credentials immediately.

title: [OPS] Connect staging services and verify deployment recovery
scope: Connect isolated Railway, optional Vercel and authorized Neon staging/production resources through safe-off GitHub deployment gates.
acceptance: Development deploys only to staging and main deploys only to production
Provider deployments remain disabled until credentials and owner acceptance exist
Record exact deployed revision and clean-session smoke evidence
No secrets in frontend/repo; rollback and migration compatibility are documented
tests: Build, workflow, flag-off/on, HTTPS, readiness, review smoke, restart and rollback tests in non-production.
risk: Accidental production changes, spending or secret exposure. Use isolated resources, bounded limits, safe-default flags and manual production promotion.

title: [QA] Verify end-to-end Arabic UX and accessibility
scope: Test the complete editor journey on desktop/mobile and keyboard/screen-reader paths.
acceptance: Intake, confirmation, report, revision and export work from a clean session
RTL, contrast, focus and non-color status communication are verified
tests: Browser E2E, keyboard walkthrough, mobile viewport and accessibility checks.
risk: Happy-path demos conceal failures. Keep failed states in the test matrix and document unresolved limits.

title: [HANDOFF] Prepare the public release and committee submission package
scope: Prepare accepted live demo, public repository, reproducible results, PDF/PPT and a video of at most two minutes.
acceptance: Owner approves history/secrets/rights review before changing visibility
Record release, artifact verification and actual final submission receipt separately
tests: Clean installation, public access, artifact/link checks and timed demonstration.
risk: Exposing secrets or misrepresenting readiness. Remain private until approved; correct artifacts before submission.

title: [LATER] Explore evidence-bounded finding discussions
scope: After MVP acceptance, evaluate discussion limited to a selected finding and its evidence bundle.
acceptance: New claims trigger a new review
No unrestricted fatwa/chat scope is introduced
tests: Evidence-boundary and topic-change tests before implementation.
risk: Scope expansion and unsupported advice. Keep disabled during MVP; revert to static explanations.

title: [LATER] Evaluate accounts, saved history and image intake
scope: Assess user need and privacy/cost for accounts, retained history and OCR only after the text-first MVP.
acceptance: Separate decisions and permissions for identity, retention and OCR
No extra personal data collected by the MVP
tests: Discovery and threat-model review; no production feature promised.
risk: Unnecessary complexity and sensitive-data collection. Defer until justified by users and a reviewed design.

title: [GOVERNANCE] Prepare judge-ready repository and secure handoff
scope: Document credential-free reproduction, official credential setup, branch/deployment gates and sanitized committee evidence without exposing internal material.
acceptance: Judge quickstart and credential guide match delivered integrations
Git workflow preserves merge history through development and main
Staging and production gates default off and no secret value is tracked
Full-history and tracked-file scans are recorded before public handoff
tests: npm run check, workflow syntax, GitHub settings read-back, credential scan and clean-clone rehearsal.
risk: A weak handoff can expose credentials or misrepresent readiness. Revoke first, keep production manual and distinguish configured from verified.
